tools.name: a11y_collapse
tools.description: Collapse a tree node / combo / disclosure by a11y name.

tools.name: a11y_expand
tools.description: Expand a tree node / combo / disclosure by a11y name (UIA ExpandCollapsePattern, AX AXExpanded).

tools.name: a11y_get_element
tools.description: Fetch a single element by accessibility name — returns name, role, bounds, value, state flags (focused/enabled/disabled/selected/busy/offscreen/expandable/expanded). Convenience singular form of find_element (which returns an array).

tools.name: a11y_get_value
tools.description: Read the current value of a named field (UIA ValuePattern / AX AXValue). Useful to verify before typing.

tools.name: a11y_list_children
tools.description: List a11y elements geometrically contained within a named parent element. Useful for enumerating menu items, tree children, dialog buttons, list rows. Matches by bounds containment — an element is a child if its rect is fully inside the parent's rect. NOT a true a11y-tree child relationship; good enough for most UI patterns.

parentName.description: Accessibility name of the parent element

controlType.description: Optional role filter on the PARENT match

tools.name: a11y_select
tools.description: Select a list item / tab / radio by a11y name (UIA SelectionItemPattern, AX AXSelected).

tools.name: a11y_toggle
tools.description: Toggle a checkbox / switch / toggle-button by a11y name. Returns new state (On/Off/Indeterminate).

tools.name: abort_task
tools.description: Signal the running task to abort. The pipeline checks `isAborted()` between steps; long-running LLM calls may take a few seconds to wind down. agent_status will return `idle` once the abort has settled.

tools.name: agent_status
tools.description: Return the autonomous agent's current state: status (idle | thinking | acting | waiting_confirm), currentTask, currentStep, stepsCompleted, stepsTotal. Cheap (synchronous read) — safe to poll at 1–2 Hz.

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run an ORDERED LIST of tool calls in one shot (collapses many round-trips into one). Each step is { name, arguments, expect? }. `name`+`arguments` is a normal tool call (compound like {"name":"computer","arguments":{"action":"type","text":"hi"}} or a granular tool). Optional `expect` is a precondition checked by RE-PERCEIVING before the step runs: {"window":"notepad"} (foreground window must match) or {"element":"Send"} (a11y element must be present). The batch HALTS on the first failed precondition, safety stop, or step error and returns a per-step trace so you re-plan from real state. Every step goes through the same safety gate as a direct call. Use `expect` to guarantee you act on the right window/element instead of guessing. Set dryRun:true to pre-scan safety tiers without executing; allowConfirm:true to let confirm-tier steps proceed.

steps.description: JSON array of ordered steps: [{ "name": "<tool>", "arguments": {...}, "expect": {"window"?,"element"?} }] (a real array is also accepted).

allowConfirm.description: Allow confirm-tier steps to run (default false → halt at them).

dryRun.description: Only report each step's safety tier; do not execute.

tools.name: build_uri
tools.description: Build a properly-encoded URI from a scheme + semantic fields. Returns the URI as text; pair with open_uri to dispatch it. Examples: scheme="mailto" + to/subject/body → RFC 6068 mailto URI. scheme="tel" + path="+15551234" → tel:+15551234. scheme="slack" + team/channel → slack URI.

scheme.description: URI scheme without the colon: mailto, tel, sms, webcal, slack, vscode, obsidian, spotify, https, etc.

path.description: Scheme-specific path (for mailto: the recipient address; for tel:/sms: the number; for https: the host+path). URL-encoded for you.

query.description: JSON object of query parameters, e.g. {"subject":"hi","body":"hello"}. Each value will be URL-encoded.

tools.name: cdp_click
tools.description: Click a page element by visible text or CSS selector (DOM click — no coordinates). Requires browser_connect first.

text.description: Visible text of the element to click (preferred).

tools.name: cdp_connect
tools.description: Open/attach a dedicated browser the agent controls via the DOM (reliable for web pages — no pixels). Call this FIRST for any website task, then use browser_navigate/read/click/type. If it fails, fall back to read_text/smart_click.

tools.name: cdp_evaluate
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the browser page context. Returns the result.

javascript.description: JavaScript code to evaluate in the page

tools.name: cdp_list_tabs
tools.description: List all open browser tabs with their URLs and titles.

tools.name: cdp_page_context
tools.description: Read the current page as structured DOM: interactive elements (links/buttons/inputs with selectors), or text for a CSS selector. Use instead of read_text on web pages. Requires browser_connect first.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector to read text from (default: structured interactive-element list for the whole page).

tools.name: cdp_read_text
tools.description: Read text content from a DOM element. Useful for extracting information from web pages.

selector.description: CSS selector (default: "body" for full page text)

tools.name: cdp_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the browser page via DOM (window.scrollBy). Works regardless of mouse position — use for reliable page scrolling.

tools.name: cdp_select_option
tools.description: Select an option in a <select> dropdown by value or visible text.

value.description: Option value or visible text to select

tools.name: cdp_switch_tab
tools.description: Switch CDP connection to a different browser tab by URL or title substring.

target.description: URL or title substring to match

tools.name: cdp_type
tools.description: Type text into a page input by CSS selector or associated label (DOM input — no coordinates). Requires browser_connect first.

label.description: Label text associated with the input (alternative to selector).

tools.name: cdp_wait_for_selector
tools.description: Wait for a DOM element matching a CSS selector to appear and become visible.

tools.name: classify_task
tools.description: Run the autonomous pipeline's preprocessor over a task description and return what it would have decided WITHOUT executing the task. External brains use this to mirror clawdcursor's routing choices: which strategy ladder (router/blind/hybrid/vision/playbook), how to decompose compound tasks into subtasks, which capability is at play (navigation/app_launch/text_input/form_fill/spatial/...), which playbook (if any) matches, the active-app guide reference, and the short telemetry reason for the choice. Pure read; zero side effects.

activeWindowTitle.description: Optional active window title for app-detection context

activeWindowProcessName.description: Optional active window process name for app-detection context

tools.name: close_window
tools.description: Polite close request (WM_CLOSE / AXCloseAction / _NET_CLOSE_WINDOW). App may prompt.

tools.name: delegate_to_agent
tools.description: **Requires the `clawdcursor agent` daemon to be running** (binds 127.0.0.1:3847). Delegates a task to clawdcursor's autonomous pipeline (runs independently with its own LLM reasoning). Returns when the task completes or times out. If you see ECONNREFUSED, start the daemon with `clawdcursor agent` and retry.

tools.name: desktop_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the entire screen, resized to 1280px wide. Returns the image and scale metadata. Use read_screen (accessibility tree) first — only screenshot when you need visual confirmation.

tools.name: desktop_screenshot_region
tools.description: Take a zoomed screenshot of a specific screen region for detailed inspection. Coordinates are in image-space (from desktop_screenshot).

x.description: Left edge X in image-space coordinates

y.description: Top edge Y in image-space coordinates

tools.name: detect_app
tools.description: Resolve a URL or window title to clawdcursor's canonical app key. Returns `{ appKey: "gmail" }` for "mail.google.com" / "Gmail - Inbox", `{ appKey: null }` when no rule matches. Pure function; same lookup the autonomous pipeline uses internally.

urlOrTitle.description: URL like "mail.google.com" or title like "Gmail - Inbox"

tools.name: detect_webview_apps
tools.description: Enumerate running Electron / WebView2 / Chromium-shell apps (e.g. New Outlook, Teams, Discord, Slack, VS Code) whose accessibility trees are typically sparse because the UI is rendered inside a web view. Returns each candidate with a CDP-discovery hint — if a remote-debugging port is already live, you can attach to it via `browser({"action":"connect"})`; otherwise the hint shows the relaunch command the user should run to enable CDP. Use this WHEN `read_screen` returns an unexpectedly empty tree on a "native" app.

tools.name: favorites_add
tools.description: Add a task string to the favorites list. No-op if already present. Returns the updated list.

tools.name: favorites_list
tools.description: Return the list of starred ("favorite") task strings. Stored locally at ~/.clawdcursor/.clawdcursor-favorites.json — never sent over the network.

tools.name: favorites_remove
tools.description: Remove a task string from the favorites list. Returns the updated list.

tools.name: find_element
tools.description: Search for UI elements by name, control type, or automation ID within a process. Returns matching elements with bounds. For browser windows with CDP attached, falls back to a DOM query when UIA returns empty so canvas / SPA content is reachable too (results are flagged with a "via CDP DOM" header and use viewport-relative coords).

tools.name: focus_element
tools.description: Keyboard-focus an element by a11y name. Does NOT raise window — use focus_window first if needed.

processId.description: Optional process id to scope the search

tools.name: focus_window
tools.description: Bring a window to the foreground. Match by processName, pid, or title substring.

tools.name: get_active_window
tools.description: Get the currently focused/foreground window.

tools.name: get_app_guide
tools.description: Return the app-knowledge guide for an app: keyboard shortcuts, workflow patterns, layout cues, tips, and the formatted prompt fragment the autonomous pipeline would inject into its LLM system prompt. External brains (editor hosts, OpenClaw, any HTTP-MCP client) call this to get the same app expertise the autonomous loop gets for free. Pass either `app` (canonical key like "gmail", "youtube") or `urlOrTitle` (the URL or window title the tool will resolve via detectApp). Returns `appKey: null` and an empty promptFragment when neither resolves.

urlOrTitle.description: URL or window title to resolve into an app key

tools.name: get_element_state
tools.description: Get state flags of a named element (focused/enabled/disabled/selected/busy/offscreen/expandable/expanded).

tools.name: get_focused_element
tools.description: Get the currently focused UI element (keyboard focus). Returns name, control type, value, bounds, and process ID.

tools.name: get_screen_size
tools.description: Get the screen dimensions and scale factor.

tools.name: get_system_prompt
tools.description: Return the canonical agent system prompt for a given strategy mode (blind / hybrid / vision). Use this to mirror clawdcursor's behavioral rules in your own agent loop — coordinate syntax, key combo syntax, web-service policy (never type "browser" into search bars), protocol escape hatches (mailto:/https:/file:/...), stagnation recovery, termination rules (done/give_up/cannot_read), untrusted-screen-content discipline. Reflects the prompt at the current installed clawdcursor version — pull this rather than hardcoding rules so they stay in sync with upstream changes.

mode.description: Agent mode: "blind" (a11y only), "hybrid" (a11y + on-demand screenshots), or "vision" (screenshot per turn)

tools.name: get_system_time
tools.description: Return the current system time as ISO 8601 UTC + local components. Zero I/O.

tools.name: get_windows
tools.description: List visible top-level windows with title, process, and bounds. Useful when the active window is wrong or missing.

tools.name: invoke_element
tools.description: Click/activate a UI element by its accessibility name. MORE RELIABLE than coord clicks — use this when the snapshot shows a named target.

automationId.description: Element automation ID (more precise than name)

controlType.description: Optional role filter (Button, MenuItem, Tab, etc.)

processId.description: Optional: limit to a specific process

tools.name: key_down
tools.description: Press a key without releasing. Pair with key_up. Use to hold modifiers (shift, ctrl) during clicks.

tools.name: key_press
tools.description: Press a key or key combo. Use "mod" for Ctrl/Cmd. Use "+" for a chord (e.g. "mod+s", "shift+Tab"). Space-separate for a sequence ("Down Down End"). Examples: "Return", "Tab", "Escape", "F5", "ctrl+a".

combo.description: Key/combo to press (e.g. "Return", "mod+s"). Space-separate for a sequence.

key.description: Alias for combo — accepted for MCP/compound backward-compatibility.

tools.name: key_up
tools.description: Release a key previously pressed with key_down.

tools.name: learn_app
tools.description: Persist a newly-learned workflow, shortcut, or tip for an app into the local guides registry. Supports merging shortcut maps and tip lists into the existing guide JSON. Use this at the end of a successful exploration so future runs can short-circuit the same task.

processName.description: Process / app name (matches an existing guide JSON file)

task.description: Optional task description that was learned

actionsJson.description: Optional JSON array of {action, …} steps that achieved the task

shortcutsJson.description: Optional JSON object of { name: keystroke } shortcut additions

tipsJson.description: Optional JSON array of free-text tips

tools.name: list_displays
tools.description: Enumerate connected displays with logical bounds + DPI ratio. Use before display-specific screenshots.

tools.name: logs_recent
tools.description: Return the last 200 captured console log entries from the daemon (level + timestamp + message). Empty array when no log buffer is attached (e.g. stdio MCP without a running daemon).

limit.description: Cap the number of entries returned (default 200)

tools.name: maximize_window
tools.description: Maximize the foreground window (or a matched window). Polite request; WM may interpret.

tools.name: minimize_window
tools.description: Minimize a window. Matches by process name, PID, or title. Cross-platform: Windows (ShowWindow), macOS (miniaturize), Linux (wmctrl/xdotool).

tools.name: minimize_window_to_taskbar
tools.description: Minimize the foreground or matched window to the taskbar / Dock.

tools.name: mouse_click
tools.description: Click at (x,y). Default coords come from the a11y snapshot (already screen-correct). If you read the target off the SCREENSHOT instead, pass space:"image" so the tool scales it. Prefer invoke_element when the target has an a11y name.

space.description: Coordinate space of the x/y you pass. "screen" (default) = accessibility-snapshot coords, already correct for the real screen. "image" = coords you read off the SCREENSHOT (downscaled to 1280px wide); the tool scales them up to the real screen. Use "image" ONLY when the target is not in the a11y snapshot and you read it off the picture.

tools.name: mouse_double_click
tools.description: Double-click the left mouse button at the given image-space coordinates.

tools.name: mouse_down
tools.description: Press a mouse button without releasing. Pair with mouse_up. Enables hold-and-drag + modifier clicks.

tools.name: mouse_drag
tools.description: Drag the mouse from (startX,startY) to (endX,endY). Used for selecting text, drawing, resizing.

space.description: Coordinate space of the x/y you pass. "screen" (default) = accessibility-snapshot coords, already correct for the real screen. "image" = coords you read off the SCREENSHOT (downscaled to 1280px wide); the tool scales them up to the real screen. Use "image" ONLY when the target is not in the a11y snapshot and you read it off the picture.

tools.name: mouse_drag_stepped
tools.description: Drag the mouse along a multi-point path in image-space. Path is a JSON string of {x,y} points. Useful for Paint-style drawing or gesture input. Press occurs at the first point and release at the last.

path.description: JSON array of {"x":n, "y":n} points in image-space, min 2 points

tools.name: mouse_hover
tools.description: Move the mouse to the given image-space coordinates without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips or hover menus.

tools.name: mouse_middle_click
tools.description: Middle-click (wheel-click) at image-space (x, y). Opens links in new tab in most browsers; pans in some apps.

tools.name: mouse_move_relative
tools.description: Move cursor by a relative offset (dx, dy). Wayland-safe via cursor cache.

tools.name: mouse_right_click
tools.description: Right-click at the given image-space coordinates (opens context menu).

tools.name: mouse_scroll
tools.description: Scroll at (x,y) in a direction. Omit x,y to scroll at the screen center.

space.description: Coordinate space of the x/y you pass. "screen" (default) = accessibility-snapshot coords, already correct for the real screen. "image" = coords you read off the SCREENSHOT (downscaled to 1280px wide); the tool scales them up to the real screen. Use "image" ONLY when the target is not in the a11y snapshot and you read it off the picture.

tools.name: mouse_scroll_horizontal
tools.description: Scroll horizontally at image-space (x, y). On Windows uses Shift+wheel synthesis; on Linux uses xdotool wheel buttons when available; on macOS uses Shift+wheel.

tools.name: mouse_triple_click
tools.description: Triple-click the left mouse button at image-space (x, y) — selects a paragraph in most text editors.

tools.name: mouse_up
tools.description: Release a mouse button previously pressed with mouse_down.

tools.name: navigate_browser
tools.description: Open a URL in the browser. Launches with CDP enabled (port 9223) for DOM interaction. Call cdp_connect after. Tier 2 (mutation): triggers network egress to an arbitrary destination + spawns/attaches to a browser process.

tools.name: ocr_read_screen
tools.description: Read all text on screen using OS-level OCR. Returns text elements with pixel coordinates (bounding boxes). Much cheaper than a screenshot — use this to find text, buttons, labels, and their positions. Coordinates are in real screen pixels.

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Open an application by name. Uses the cross-OS app alias table + the PlatformAdapter's launchApp (UWP-aware on Windows, `open -a` on macOS, gtk-launch / xdg-open on Linux).

tools.name: open_file
tools.description: Open a file or folder in the OS default application. Uses `open` (macOS), `xdg-open` (Linux), and explorer / ShellExecute (Windows). Tier 2 (mutation): on some platforms "opening" a file may execute it (.exe on Windows, .app on macOS, scripts with executable bit on Linux), and the registered handler can be privileged or destructive.

tools.name: open_uri
tools.description: Open ANY registered URI (mailto:, tel:, sms:, webcal:, file:, slack:, vscode:, obsidian:, spotify:, zoommtg:, https:, custom-scheme:, ...) via the OS protocol-handler registry. The OS routes to whichever app the user has registered as the handler. Replaces dozens of app-specific shortcuts with one general primitive. For mailto:, use the convenience helper compose_uri_mailto, or pass a full pre-built URI. Tier 2 (mutation): the OS will dispatch to whatever app is registered for the scheme — that handler may be privileged or destructive (file: opens files which on Windows can execute .exe; vscode: opens a workspace; zoommtg: joins a call). The dispatcher does no scheme allowlist — callers + the agent loop are responsible for not constructing dangerous URIs.

uri.description: A full URI like "mailto:bob@example.com?subject=hi&body=hello", "tel:+15551234", "slack://channel?team=T123&id=C456", "vscode://file/Users/me/code/x.ts", "https://example.com". Must be properly URL-encoded.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Open a URL in the OS default browser. Non-browser-agnostic counterpart to navigate_browser. Tier 1 (input): triggers network egress and may launch the registered HTTP handler (which can be any app, not strictly a browser). Downgraded from tier 2 in 0.9.4 (issue #101 bug 3) because an agent host can always reach the same primitive via Bash (`open <url>` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux, `start <url>` on Windows) — the tier-2 gate added friction without preventing the action. URL must start with http(s)://.

tools.name: read_clipboard
tools.description: Read the current text content of the OS clipboard.

tools.name: read_screen
tools.description: Refresh the accessibility snapshot of the focused window (already attached each turn — call this only if you suspect staleness).

processId.description: Optional: limit to a specific process

tools.name: relaunch_with_cdp
tools.description: Relaunch a WebView2 / Electron app with a remote-debugging port enabled so `browser` tools can attach. The relaunch closes the existing instance (asks the OS to close politely via window_close first), then starts a new one with `--remote-debugging-port=<port>`. The user MUST consent — this WILL lose any unsaved work in the app. Returns instructions + the new port. Prefer the hint from `detect_webview_apps` when possible.

port.description: Port to open for CDP. Default 9222.

tools.name: resize_window
tools.description: Set the foreground (or matched) window bounds in logical pixels. Omitted fields preserved.

tools.name: restore_window
tools.description: Restore a minimized or maximized window to its previous bounds.

tools.name: scheduled_task_create
tools.description: Create a recurring task that runs on a cron schedule. The task submits to the autonomous agent each time the cron tick fires; if the agent is busy at that moment, the tick is skipped (no queue). Cron is standard 5-field syntax (`* * * * *` = every minute) or 6-field with leading seconds. Returns the created task with id + next-run timestamp. Persisted across daemon restarts.

task.description: Natural-language task to run on each tick

tz.description: Optional timezone (e.g. "America/New_York"). Defaults to server local.

tools.name: scheduled_task_delete
tools.description: Delete one scheduled task by id. No-op if id is unknown.

tools.name: scheduled_task_list
tools.description: Return every scheduled task: id, cron expression, task text, enabled state, run/skip counters, last-run / last-error, next-run timestamp.

tools.name: scheduled_task_toggle
tools.description: Pause/resume a scheduled task without deleting it. When disabled the cron job is unregistered (no firing); state stays persisted.

tools.name: screenshot_full
tools.description: Capture the full primary display. Returns base64 image bytes plus a `format` field (`jpeg` by default, `png` if configured); the MCP `image.mimeType` is set to match. Equivalent to desktop_screenshot but returns the full frame unconditionally (no region cropping). Useful for the dashboard's /screenshot REST replacement.

tools.name: set_field_value
tools.description: Set an editable field's value directly via accessibility (more reliable than click+type for forms).

tools.name: shortcuts_execute
tools.description: Execute a keyboard shortcut by describing what you want to do (e.g. "scroll down", "close tab", "upvote"). Uses fuzzy matching against the shortcuts database. Provide context (active app name) for app-specific shortcuts like Reddit or Outlook.

intent.description: What you want to do (e.g. "scroll down", "new tab", "copy", "upvote", "reply to email")

context.description: Active app context for app-specific shortcuts (e.g. "reddit", "outlook"). Auto-detected from active window if omitted.

tools.name: shortcuts_list
tools.description: List available keyboard shortcuts. Filter by category (navigation, browser, editing, social, window, file, view, quick) and/or context (e.g. "reddit", "outlook"). Returns shortcut names, descriptions, and key combos for the current platform. Use this BEFORE reaching for mouse_scroll or mouse_click — there is often a faster keyboard shortcut.

category.description: Filter by category: navigation, browser, editing, social, window, file, view, quick. Omit to list all.

context.description: Filter by app context (e.g. "reddit", "outlook", "x.com"). Shows context-specific shortcuts that match.

tools.name: smart_click
tools.description: Click a UI element by name with automatic fallback. OCR-first: scans screen text and clicks by coordinates. Also tries a11y invoke (in parallel) and CDP as fallbacks. No screenshot or coordinate math needed — just provide the element text.

target.description: Element name/text to click (e.g., "Send", "Submit", "New Email"). Alias: "name".

name.description: Alias for "target" — the rest of the accessibility surface uses "name".

processId.description: Limit search to a specific process

tools.name: smart_read
tools.description: Read text from the screen with automatic fallback. OCR-first pipeline: runs OCR (primary) and a11y tree (supplement) in parallel. Returns structured text without needing a screenshot. Use this as your primary perception tool.

scope.description: Read scope: "focused" for focused element, "window" for active window, "screen" for full screen

target.description: Element name to read from specifically. Alias: "name".

tools.name: smart_type
tools.description: Type text into a UI element. If target is specified, finds and focuses the element first. Uses clipboard paste for reliability (no dropped characters).

target.description: Element name to focus before typing (optional — types into currently focused element if omitted). Alias: "name".

processId.description: Limit search to a specific process

tools.name: submit_report
tools.description: Submit a redacted task-log report to clawdcursor's telemetry endpoint. Opt-in only — never runs unless explicitly invoked. Returns the server-issued report ID and a preview of the redacted payload, or an error reason when submission fails.

userNote.description: Optional free-text note describing what went wrong

logIndex.description: Index into the recent task logs (0 = most recent). Defaults to 0.

tools.name: submit_task
tools.description: Submit a natural-language task to the autonomous agent. The agent classifies, decomposes, and executes the task through the unified pipeline (a11y → text-agent → vision fallback). Returns immediately with `accepted: true`; poll agent_status to track progress. Runs locally on a cheap model — prefer this over driving the mouse_*/screenshot tools yourself to save tokens.

tools.name: switch_tab_os
tools.description: Cycle or jump to a browser tab using the OS-agnostic keyboard shortcut (mod+Tab / mod+Shift+Tab / mod+{1..9}). Works in Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari. For in-browser DOM-level control use cdp_switch_tab.

index.description: Jump to tab N (1-based, 1-9). If omitted, direction must be provided.

direction.description: Cycle "next" or "previous". Ignored when `index` is given.

tools.name: task_logs_current
tools.description: Return the structured log entries for the currently-executing task (or the most recent if no task is running). Each entry is a JSONL event from the pipeline trace.

tools.name: task_logs_list
tools.description: List the last 50 task summaries from the daemon's structured log. Each summary contains task text, correlation ID, start/end timestamps, and final status. Returns [] when no logger is attached.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type text into the currently focused input. Prefer set_field_value when a field has an a11y name.

tools.name: undo_last
tools.description: Send the OS Undo keystroke (mod+Z).

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Wait for a specified duration. Useful after animations or page loads.

tools.name: wait_for_element
tools.description: Poll the a11y tree until an element matching name/controlType appears. Useful after an action spawns a dialog.

processId.description: Scope the search to a process

tools.name: write_clipboard
tools.description: Write text to the OS clipboard. Tier 2 (mutation): overwrites the user's clipboard, which can hijack subsequent copy/paste flows. Reversibility is via a fresh user-initiated copy, not by the agent.
